dialogue_refs.speaker: C-01
dialogue_refs.delivery: Address the crouching survivors without raising the voice. Separate the three instructions cleanly, making each one final and immediately actionable.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-04
dialogue_refs.delivery: Touch the radio as the question is asked. Mahmoud needs one precise decision before the groups separate, not reassurance.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-01
dialogue_refs.delivery: Answer Mahmoud directly, with a slight beat after «مَعَاكْ». Land «وِمَقْفُولْ» as an order that permits no radio transmission.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-03
dialogue_refs.emotion: exhausted generosity masked by a weak lie
dialogue_refs.delivery: Offer the canteen with barely enough breath to speak. Try to make the lie sound casual, because admitting thirst might make Mahmoud refuse.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-04
dialogue_refs.delivery: Hold Mostafa’s gaze and let the single word carry recognition of Sayed. Keep it dry and intimate, with no sentimental emphasis.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-12
dialogue_refs.delivery: Reading her brother's letter aloud to her mother, not knowing if he is alive.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-03
dialogue_refs.emotion: brave reassurance giving way to need
dialogue_refs.delivery: He is composing the letter to calm his mother, keeping a young man's steady warmth through the family details. On «ادْعِيلِي كِتِيرْ», let the courage thin slightly without breaking into fear.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-12
dialogue_refs.delivery: She reads the date, makes the connection, then tells her mother without looking away from the page. Leave a small stunned gap before the final phrase; do not sob.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-11
dialogue_refs.delivery: She gives the letter back as if hearing his words again can keep him present. It is a mother's insistence, not a barked command, with no visible collapse.

dialogue_refs.speaker: INFANTRY SENTRY
dialogue_refs.delivery: Challenge the distant figures while keeping the rifle trained on them. The fear is controlled by sentry discipline, not played as panic.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-01
dialogue_refs.delivery: Force the single word across the flat through a dry, damaged throat. Keep it clipped and authoritative; Shalabi is identifying his men and stopping a fatal mistake.

beats.title: The son returns

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-12
dialogue_refs.delivery: Call to Mostafa first as recognition bursts out, then throw «يَامَّا» back toward the house while running. Keep the voice recognizably a twelve-year-old's, breathless but not shrill.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-11
dialogue_refs.delivery: Barely a whisper, touching his face; she cannot believe he is real.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-03
dialogue_refs.delivery: Look toward the oven because speaking directly about the reunion is too difficult. Let the question catch slightly, with a young man's weighted voice rather than a child's vulnerability.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-11
dialogue_refs.delivery: Answer him at close range, smiling through tears without turning the line into a punchline. «كُلّْ يُومْ» should reveal her private ritual simply, not ask for pity.

beats.title: Sayed's letter

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-03
dialogue_refs.delivery: At her door, holding out the letter; he has carried this for days and can barely say it.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-02
dialogue_refs.delivery: Read it as words Sayed wrote practically before danger, not as a ghost speaking from beyond death. Stay plain and intimate, allowing only «وِأَنَا مِشْ نَدْمَانْ» to carry a quiet final release.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-14
dialogue_refs.delivery: Ali looks directly at Mostafa and asks the literal question he needs answered. Keep it small and unperformed, with no adult understanding added to the child’s voice.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-03
dialogue_refs.delivery: At the boy’s height, Mostafa gives him one firm truth and one kindness. Hold Ali’s gaze and resist smiling or sounding falsely cheerful.

dialogue_refs.speaker: C-13
dialogue_refs.delivery: Fatma steps aside and addresses Mostafa almost maternally, accepting both him and what he has brought. Keep the words steady; the effort not to cry should register only in the breath.
